title: REIT、苦境下で「攻めの増資」　分配金成長に市場冷ややか
extracted_text:
不動産投資信託（REIT）の増資が相次いでいる。2026年に入って増資した8銘柄が調達した合計額は、25年通年の全体の調達額を上回った。REITの増資は物件取得に向けた「攻め」の戦略といえる。しかし市場の評価は芳しくはない。

「好ましくない増資が増えないかと心配している」。三井住友DSアセットマネジメントの倉島克彦シニアファンドマネージャーは浮かない表情を見せる。

市場で話題になった増資の一つがオフィス特化型の グローバル・ワン不動産投資法人 。3月25日に最大157億円を調達して都内と千葉市の2物件を取得すると発表した。運用会社のグローバル・アライアンス・リアルティの山崎弦IR部長は「長期的に分配金成長につながるとみて取得を決めた」と説明する。だが翌日の投資口価格（株価に相当）は5%下げた。

グローバル・ワンは26年9月期と27年3月期の1口あたり分配金予想を3200円としたが、売却益などを除いた1口あたり利益は27年3月期にかけ減少する。千葉市の物件の一部テナントでレントホリデー（契約期間のうち特定期間の賃料が免除される）条項があることなどが理由だが「都内の取得物件も築年数が古く、成長性や物件の質に疑問を持つ投資家は多かった」（東海東京インテリジェンス・ラボの中村貴司シニアREITアナリスト）との声も聞かれる。

同じく3月に増資で最大152億円を調達し沖縄のホテルなどを取得すると発表した Oneリート投資法人 も、翌日の投資口価格は6%安となった。中国地方の運用会社のファンドマネージャーは「取得したホテルは改修を要する。元々オフィス特化型のREITであり、本当に成長させられるとの確信を持てない」と話す。

今年に入り増資を発表した銘柄の投資口価格は総じてさえない。特に厳しい評価につながった事例で共通するのが、投資口価格が低迷する中での「ディスカウント増資」だ。NAV倍率（株式のPBR=株価純資産倍率=に相当）が1倍を切る状態で増資をすれば、投資口あたりの価値の希薄化や口数増加による需給の悪化が意識されやすい。

増資が相次ぐ背景には、REIT業界での積極的な物件取得による成長を目指す機運の高まりがある。25年は保有物件を売却し分配金に充てる動きが増え、東証REIT指数は年間で2割上昇した。NAV倍率が1倍を超える銘柄も増え「26年は増資による物件取得やそれに伴う分配金の増加期待もテーマ」（SMBC日興証券の鳥井裕史シニアアナリスト）と目されていた。

一方でNAV倍率が1倍未満で規模が比較的小さいREITは、保有物件を入れ替える余地が乏しい。増資で物件を取得し賃料収入を引き上げないと分配金を維持しにくい。岡三証券の並木幹郎シニアアナリストは「投資主価値を毀損しても、増資による規模拡大に頼らざるを得ない面がある」と話す。

REITは増資で魅力的な物件を取得し、物件の含み益を顕在化しつつ資産規模を拡大するのが本来の成長の姿だ。増資をしても市場の評価は下がらないREITもある。

例えば今年1月に増資で227億円を調達した 日本ビルファンド投資法人 は、スポンサーの 三井不動産 から中央区・日本橋のオフィスなどを取得。来期の1口あたり分配金・利益ともに今期から増加を見込む。公表後の投資口価格はおおむねプラス圏で推移した。

26年に入りREITの収益環境は厳しくなりつつある。国内長期金利の指標である新発10年物国債利回りは2.4%台に上昇。不動産価格も上昇が続いており「分配金成長につながる物件を取得する難易度は高まっている」とニッセイ基礎研究所の岩佐浩人上席研究員は指摘する。

3〜4月に決算を発表したREITでは分配金予想を見直すケースも相次いだ。 三菱地所物流リート投資法人 は4月に分配金の目標について、従来は年3.5%以上の成長としていたのを、2936円程度を当面維持すると変更した。一時的なテナントの退去や想定を上回る金利コストの増加が理由だ。

国内のREITは58本あるが、NAV倍率が1倍を上回るのはまだ少数派。苦境下の増資で投資口価格がかえって下がれば、市場での選別は加速する。みずほ信託銀行の小川剛宏氏は「投資口価格の低迷が続くREITは再編が選択肢になりやすい」と指摘する。増資ブームが業界の再編機運を高めるかもしれない。

（杵渕純平）

translated_text:
Japanese Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) have been rushing to conduct capital increases. The combined amount raised by eight issuers that conducted capital increases since the start of 2026 has already surpassed the total amount raised throughout all of 2025. REIT capital increases can be seen as a 'proactive' strategy for acquiring properties. However, the market's response has been less than enthusiastic.

'There are concerns that unwanted capital increases could keep coming.' Kurashima Katsuhiko, a senior fund manager at Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management, showed an uneasy expression.

One capital increase that sparked discussion in the market was by office-focused Global One Real Estate Investment Corporation. On March 25, it announced plans to raise up to 15.7 billion yen to acquire two properties in central Tokyo and Chiba City. Yamasaki Tsuyoshi, head of the IR department at parent company Global Alliance Realty, explained, 'We decided to acquire these properties because we see them leading to long-term dividend growth.' Yet the investment unit price (equivalent to a stock price) fell 5% the following day.

Global One projected per-unit dividends of 3,200 yen for the fiscal periods ending September 2026 and March 2027. However, profit per unit excluding gains from property sales is expected to decline through March 2027. This is partly due to rent holiday clauses at some tenants in the Chiba City property, where rent is waived for a specified period during the contract term. One analyst noted, 'Many investors questioned the growth potential and quality of the Tokyo property as well, given its age.' Nakamura Takashi, a senior REIT analyst at Tokai Tokyo Intelligence Lab, pointed out that 'there were many investors who had doubts.'

One REIT Investment Corporation, which announced in March that it would raise up to 15.2 billion yen through a capital increase to acquire hotels in Okinawa, also saw its investment unit price drop 6% the next day. A fund manager at a Chugoku region REIT operator said, 'The hotels we acquired need renovation. This is fundamentally an office-focused REIT, and I'm not convinced it can truly drive growth.'

Investment unit prices for issuers that announced capital increases this year have generally been underperforming. The common factor in cases receiving particularly harsh market criticism has been 'dilutive capital increases' amid低迷 unit prices. When capital increases are conducted while NAV multiples (equivalent to P/B ratio for stocks) fall below 1x, concerns about per-unit value dilution and supply-demand deterioration from increased unit counts become prominent.

The background to this wave of capital increases stems from a growing momentum in the REIT industry to pursue growth through aggressive property acquisitions. In 2025, the practice of selling held properties to fund dividends increased, and the Tokyo Stock Exchange REIT Index rose 20% for the year. With more issuers trading above NAV multiples, 'expectations for property acquisitions through capital increases and the resulting dividend increases became a theme for 2026,' according to Torii Hirofumi, a senior analyst at SMBC Nikko Securities.

On the other hand, smaller REITs with NAV multiples below 1x have limited room to swap properties. Without acquiring properties through capital increases to boost rental income, maintaining dividends becomes difficult. Namiki Mikio, a senior analyst at Okasan Securities, said, 'There are cases where issuers have no choice but to rely on capital increases for scale expansion, even if it damages unitholder value.'

The original growth model for REITs involves acquiring attractive properties through capital increases, realizing unrealized gains, and expanding asset size. However, some REITs see their valuations decline even after capital increases, while others do not.

For example, Japan Building Fund Investment Corporation raised 22.7 billion yen through a capital increase in January this year to acquire office properties in Chuo Ward, Nihonbashi from sponsor Mitsui Fudosan. It expects increases in both per-unit dividends and earnings in the next fiscal period compared to the current one. Investment unit prices have generally trended positively since the announcement.

Since the start of 2026, the revenue environment for REITs has been tightening. The benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield, a key indicator of domestic long-term interest rates, has risen to around 2.4%. Property prices have also continued climbing, and 'the difficulty of acquiring properties that will drive dividend growth is increasing,' according to Iwasaka Hiroto, a senior researcher at NLI Research Institute.

REITs reporting earnings in March and April have also been revising dividend forecasts. Mitsubishi Estate Logistics REIT Investment Corporation changed its dividend target in April from an annual growth rate of 3.5% or more to maintaining a level of around 2,936 yen for the foreseeable future. The reasons included temporary tenant departures and interest cost increases exceeding assumptions.

Of the 58 domestic REITs, only a minority trade above NAV multiples. If capital increases amid difficult conditions cause investment unit prices to decline further, market selection will accelerate. Ogawa Takehiro of Mizuho Trust Bank noted, 'REITs with persistently depressed unit prices are likely to become candidates for consolidation.' The capital increase boom may end up fueling industry restructuring.
title_en: REITs Pursue 'Aggressive Capital Raises' Amid Challenges, But Market Remains Skeptical of Dividend Growth
